questions.prompt: Who sculpted The Thinker?
questions.hint: The work was conceived in connection with The Gates of Hell.
questions.explanation: Auguste Rodin created The Thinker.

questions.prompt: What nickname is commonly used for the Academy Award statuette?
questions.hint: The award honors film achievement.
questions.explanation: The Academy Award statuette is commonly called an Oscar.

questions.prompt: How many strings does a standard guitar usually have?
questions.hint: The most common tuning runs E-A-D-G-B-E.
questions.explanation: A standard guitar usually has six strings.

questions.prompt: Who wrote Alice's Adventures in Wonderland?
questions.hint: The author's real name was Charles Dodgson.
questions.explanation: Lewis Carroll wrote Alice's Adventures in Wonderland.

questions.prompt: Tango developed primarily around the Río de la Plata, especially in Argentina and which other country?
questions.hint: Montevideo shares the tradition with Buenos Aires.
questions.explanation: Tango developed in the urban culture of Argentina and Uruguay.

questions.prompt: Who composed the opera Carmen?
questions.hint: The opera includes the Habanera.
questions.explanation: Georges Bizet composed Carmen.

questions.prompt: A montage sequence often serves what purpose?

choices.text: Showing one uncut real-time action only
Compressing time or conveying a series of developments

questions.hint: Training sequences often use it.
questions.explanation: Montage can condense many events into a short screen duration.

questions.prompt: Art Nouveau is especially known for what visual quality?
questions.hint: Plant-like curves are common.
questions.explanation: Art Nouveau favors sinuous, natural forms and decorative integration.

questions.prompt: Stream-of-consciousness writing tries to represent what?

choices.text: The flow of a character's thoughts and perceptions

questions.hint: It may follow associative mental movement.
questions.explanation: Stream of consciousness imitates the continuous movement of inner experience.

questions.prompt: The circle of fifths organizes what?
questions.hint: Moving around it changes the key by a perfect fifth.
questions.explanation: The circle of fifths maps key signatures and harmonic relationships.

questions.prompt: What does mise-en-scène refer to?

choices.text: The arrangement of visual elements within the filmed scene

questions.hint: Sets, lighting, costume, and blocking are included.
questions.explanation: Mise-en-scène describes what is placed before the camera and how it is arranged.

questions.prompt: Tenebrism is characterized by what?

choices.text: Dramatic darkness with sharply illuminated areas

questions.hint: Caravaggio is closely associated with it.
questions.explanation: Tenebrism uses extreme contrasts between darkness and concentrated light.

questions.prompt: What is an unreliable narrator?

choices.text: A narrator who speaks only in rhyme
A narrator whose account cannot be fully trusted
A narrator who knows every fact accurately

questions.hint: Bias, deception, or limited understanding may distort the story.
questions.explanation: An unreliable narrator presents a questionable or incomplete version of events.

questions.prompt: Which composer is most associated with developing the twelve-tone method?
questions.hint: The method organizes all twelve chromatic pitches.
questions.explanation: Arnold Schoenberg developed the twelve-tone technique.

questions.prompt: What is iconoclasm?

choices.text: The rejection or destruction of religious images

questions.hint: The term combines image and breaker.
questions.explanation: Iconoclasm is opposition to or destruction of sacred images.

questions.prompt: What is a smoke alarm designed to detect?
questions.hint: It warns of a possible fire.
questions.explanation: Smoke alarms detect smoke or related particles and sound an alert.

questions.prompt: Why does refrigeration help preserve food?

choices.text: It slows microbial growth and chemical reactions

questions.hint: Lower temperatures reduce reaction rates.
questions.explanation: Refrigeration slows spoilage processes.

questions.prompt: What is a receipt?

choices.text: A record that payment or a transaction occurred

questions.hint: Stores issue it after purchase.
questions.explanation: A receipt documents a transaction and payment.

questions.prompt: Two-factor authentication requires what?

choices.text: Two different kinds of authentication evidence
Two copies of the same password

questions.hint: A password plus a phone code is a common example.
questions.explanation: 2FA combines distinct factors such as knowledge and possession.

questions.prompt: A magnetic compass needle points roughly toward which direction?
questions.hint: Earth's magnetic field aligns it.
questions.explanation: A compass aligns with Earth's magnetic field and points toward magnetic north.

questions.prompt: Dehydration means the body lacks enough what?
questions.hint: It can follow heavy sweating without fluid replacement.
questions.explanation: Dehydration is an excessive loss or shortage of body water.

questions.prompt: In finance, amortization commonly means what?

choices.text: Spreading repayment or cost over time

questions.hint: Many mortgages use scheduled principal payments.
questions.explanation: Amortization allocates a balance or cost across periods.

questions.prompt: Baking soda is the common name for what compound?
questions.hint: It releases carbon dioxide when reacted with acid.
questions.explanation: Baking soda is sodium bicarbonate.

questions.prompt: What is phishing?

choices.text: A way to cool a processor
Fraudulent impersonation used to steal information

questions.hint: Fake emails often mimic trusted organizations.
questions.explanation: Phishing tricks users into revealing credentials or data.

questions.prompt: In insurance, what is a deductible?

choices.text: The amount the insured pays before coverage applies

questions.hint: Higher deductibles often lower premiums.
questions.explanation: A deductible is the initial covered loss borne by the policyholder.

questions.prompt: A fiduciary is required to act primarily in whose interest?
questions.hint: The relationship imposes a duty of loyalty and care.
questions.explanation: A fiduciary must act for the benefit of the party to whom the duty is owed.

questions.prompt: What does zoning regulate?

choices.text: How land and buildings may be used

questions.hint: It can separate residential, commercial, and industrial uses.
questions.explanation: Zoning rules govern land use and development.

questions.prompt: What is the placebo effect?

choices.text: A change associated with expectations or the treatment context rather than the active intervention alone

questions.hint: It complicates clinical trials.
questions.explanation: Placebo effects are responses produced by expectations and contextual factors.

questions.prompt: What makes compound interest different from simple interest?
questions.hint: Each period may build on prior accumulated interest.
questions.explanation: Compound interest is calculated on principal plus previously earned interest.

questions.prompt: Bond duration is primarily used to estimate sensitivity to changes in what?
questions.hint: Longer duration usually means greater price sensitivity.
questions.explanation: Duration approximates how a bond's price responds to yield changes.

sets.title: Arts and Culture
sets.description: A mixed set covering painting, sculpture, literature, film, music, performance, and critical terminology.

sets.title: Everyday Expert
sets.description: A mixed practical-knowledge set that starts with familiar household ideas and ends with sophisticated legal and financial concepts.
